prompt: In `EarlyStopping.__init__` (`lightning/pytorch/callbacks/early_stopping.py`): the `patience` parameter accepts 0 and negative integers. A `patience=0` stops training immediately on the first check; negative values are silently nonsensical. Add a validation guard — raise `MisconfigurationException` with message `'patience must be >= 1, got <value>'` if `patience < 1`. The existing `mode` validation at the bottom of `__init__` shows the pattern to follow.

In `EarlyStopping.__init__` (`lightning/pytorch/callbacks/early_stopping.py`): the `min_delta` parameter accepts negative values. A negative `min_delta` effectively inverts the improvement criterion (the stopping condition becomes easier to meet than the user intended). Add a validation guard — raise `MisconfigurationException` with message `'min_delta must be >= 0, got <value>'` if `min_delta < 0`. Place it near the existing `mode` validation.

In `ModelCheckpoint._save_checkpoint` (`lightning/pytorch/callbacks/model_checkpoint.py`): the method is sometimes called multiple times within the same global step. Add a guard at the top of `_save_checkpoint`: if `trainer.global_step == self._last_global_step_saved`, call `rank_zero_info` to log that the duplicate save is being skipped and return early without saving. The field `self._last_global_step_saved` already exists and is updated at the end of the method.

In `ModelCheckpoint.__init__` (`lightning/pytorch/callbacks/model_checkpoint.py`): `save_top_k=0` silently disables all checkpoint saving, which is almost always a misconfiguration rather than deliberate. After the existing `save_top_k < -1` validation (which raises `MisconfigurationException`), add a separate warning — call `rank_zero_warn` with message `'ModelCheckpoint(save_top_k=0) is set: no checkpoints will be saved. Pass save_top_k=-1 to save all checkpoints.'` when `save_top_k == 0`.
